entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Clearchus of Heraclea (b. unknown, d. 351 BCE) was a Classical Greek philosopher and thinker whose significance lies in his contributions to the development of Stoic philosophy.




Clearchus was born in Heraclea, a city in ancient Greece, and his life and works had a profound impact on the intellectual landscape of the Hellenistic era. His philosophical ideas, although not as widely known as those of his contemporaries, such as Zeno of Citium, have had a lasting influence on Western philosophy.





Clearchus' most notable work, 'On Virtue', presents a comprehensive and systematic account of Stoic ethics, emphasizing the importance of reason, self-control, and indifference to external events. His writings also demonstrate a strong emphasis on the role of individual virtue in achieving happiness and fulfillment.






The legacy of Clearchus can be seen in the development of Stoic schools and the influence of his ideas on later philosophers, such as Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius. His philosophical contributions continue to be studied and debated by scholars today, offering valuable insights into the development of Western philosophy and the human condition.






In the words of Epictetus, 'Clearchus was a great man, and his teachings are still worth reading today'.
